deckTitle: IGNORE DYSTOPIA — Anatomy of a Trap (Deck B)

cards.power: Set a public timer near midnight and move the hands by announcement, never by event.
cards.lore: A symbol of danger adjusted by judgment reads as objective measurement to the public.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the midnight-hand bureaucrat. Role, action, and audience all immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink editorial. Subject: robed figure moving clock hands by decree. Mood: bureaucratic menace.

cards.power: Keep the catastrophe permanently arriving and never arrived.
cards.lore: The fear tracks the coverage, not the actual events.
cards.gradeReason: Action is the card: perpetual arrival, never landing. Crystal performative role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda illustration. Subject: disaster eternally approaching horizon but never landing. Mood: frozen dread.

cards.power: Convert the citizen into an audience by giving them a clock they cannot stop.
cards.lore: Heavy exposure to dramatized danger correlates with withdrawal and mistrust.
cards.gradeReason: Two clear roles in one card: the converter and the frozen convert. Both instantly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink wash. Subject: citizen-audience frozen before unstoppable doomsday clock. Mood: paralyzed spectatorship.

cards.power: When one deadline passes, issue the next at full volume and never acknowledge the expiration.
cards.lore: The fear is the renewable product, not the forecast.
cards.gradeReason: Precise procedural instruction: let it expire silently, reissue louder. Zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: retro broadcast parody. Subject: expired alarm relabeled and reissued at full shriek. Mood: renewable urgency.

cards.power: Declare an emergency large enough to suspend normal rules and sell the suspension as care.
cards.lore: Moments of crisis push through measures the public is too disoriented to resist.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the emergency-declaring authority. Declare, suspend, reframe as care. Immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink editorial. Subject: suited figure pulling emergency lever, selling the power grab as protection. Mood: manufactured hysteria.

cards.power: Install the exception as temporary and promise it ends when the danger does.
cards.lore: The exception tends to become the rule, outlasting the crisis that birthed it.
cards.gradeReason: Install, promise, outlast. Three-beat performance script. Perfect G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda woodcut. Subject: TEMPORARY stamp becoming permanent fixture in law book. Mood: bureaucratic creep.

cards.power: Keep the threat alive so the powers never have to be handed back.
cards.lore: Institutions empowered by an emergency acquire a structural incentive for it to continue.
cards.gradeReason: Role is the feeding loop: threat feeds power, power feeds threat. Immediate ouroboros.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic ink. Subject: institution feeding the emergency that feeds the institution, ouroboros loop. Mood: structural malice.

cards.power: Let yesterday's exception become today's standing furniture.
cards.lore: Normalization is the slow acceptance of the unthinkable through tiny, waved-through steps.
cards.gradeReason: Passive 'let' softens the role — player must infer they are the normalizer, not named actor.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical illustration. Subject: yesterday's emergency measure installed as everyday furniture, citizen shrugging. Mood: resigned normalization.

cards.gradeReason: No POWER/LORE text — fully visual card (elephant spraying LIES/FAKE NEWS/CHAOS). Concept clear, instruction absent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaotic editorial cartoon. Subject: authority elephant spraying firehose of contradictory lies at overwhelmed snail. Mood: designed disorientation.

cards.power: Flood the field so attention becomes the scarce resource, then ration it.
cards.lore: A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.
cards.gradeReason: Flood, make scarce, ration. Perfect three-move game action sequence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: information flood reducing attention to rationed drops in begging bowl. Mood: manufactured scarcity.

cards.power: Exhaust the sorting mind until the tired sorter accepts the default.
cards.lore: Repeated decisions degrade the quality of later ones via decision fatigue.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the choice-fatiguer. Exhaust until acceptance. Sharp and direct.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: exhausted brain sieve accepting worst option after overload of decisions. Mood: depleted compliance.

cards.power: Overload the reader until they gratefully accept whatever floats to the top.
cards.lore: Structural filters shape what reaches the public without needing a central censor.
cards.gradeReason: Overload, then gratitude, then acceptance. Elegant dark operator arc, immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical illustration. Subject: content-flooded reader reaching gratefully for whatever surfaces. Mood: managed passivity.

cards.power: Install a voice whose job is to be worried on schedule with camera-ready confidence.
cards.lore: Confident, media-friendly forecasters are often the least accurate but best choice.
cards.gradeReason: Character sketch so specific the player inhabits it immediately: worried, scheduled, camera-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink caricature. Subject: parrot in pundit suit, perpetually alarmed, perpetually booked. Mood: performative expertise.

cards.power: Borrow authority so the claim travels without its evidence attached.
cards.lore: Assertions move through a crowd on the strength of a title, leaving the proof at home.
cards.gradeReason: Borrow, detach, travel. One clean action that player can immediately perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: title badge propelling claim forward while evidence stays behind locked door. Mood: borrowed authority.

cards.power: Reward confident prediction and never compare it to what actually happened.
cards.lore: Pundit ecosystems keep no score, so being wrong carries zero cost.
cards.gradeReason: Systemic description of ecosystem incentives rather than a direct player performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical scoreboard. Subject: pundit trophy case with zero accuracy, full booking schedule. Mood: accountability vacuum.

cards.power: Reward the loudly wrong with another segment; volume is the only metric.
cards.lore: Media incentives select for attention-generation regardless of their accuracy record.
cards.gradeReason: Player IS the booker. Volume metric makes the decision rule instant and embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: broadcast parody. Subject: wrong pundit handed next booking trophy, volume meter maxed. Mood: amplified wrongness.

cards.power: Build a trough with no bottom and call it staying informed.
cards.lore: Variable, unpredictable rewards produce the most persistent, slot-machine-like behavior.
cards.gradeReason: Build a bottomless trough and rename it journalism. Architect role is immediate and sinister.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark editorial. Subject: slot machine disguised as news feed with no visible floor. Mood: compulsive emptiness.

cards.power: Charge a little adrenaline per scroll and collect it all day.
cards.lore: The mind weighs bad more heavily than good; feeds optimized for engagement exploit this bias.
cards.gradeReason: Player is the adrenaline tax collector. Collect per scroll. Dark and immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: economic satire. Subject: adrenaline coin collected at each scroll tollbooth, harvested all day. Mood: biological arbitrage.

cards.power: Let watching together feel like acting together.
cards.lore: Low-cost online gestures substitute for meaningful action, mistaking shared attention for shared movement.
cards.gradeReason: Passive 'let' again — diagnostic observation of herd, not a direct performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: crowd staring at shared screen, mistaking paralysis for coordination. Mood: shared inertia.

cards.power: Harvest paralysis; it monetizes better than action ever would.
cards.lore: When attention is the product, the system optimizes for the outrage that holds the eye best.
cards.gradeReason: Harvest paralysis. Player is the yield farmer of human stillness. Immediately dark and clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark harvest illustration. Subject: combine harvester reaping viewer paralysis as cash crop. Mood: monetized inaction.

cards.power: Insist the moment to act already passed, because grief is quieter than effort.
cards.lore: Doomism demobilizes people as effectively as outright denial.
cards.gradeReason: Insist it's too late. Sell grief over effort. Crisp, dark, immediately performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic ink. Subject: sealed window with past moment visible outside, grief-seller inside. Mood: manufactured bereavement.

cards.power: Frame any effort as waste, since the outcome is fixed.
cards.lore: When people believe an outcome is determined, they withdraw, making the prophecy self-fulfilling.
cards.gradeReason: Frame effort as waste. Self-fulfilling prophecy machine. Player role is the framer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fatalist editorial. Subject: figure abandoning bucket mid-bail because outcome is certified as fixed. Mood: self-fulfilling surrender.

cards.power: Offer certain defeat as relief; it asks nothing of you.
cards.lore: Certainty of disaster reduces the discomfort of ambiguity, making fatalism feel restful.
cards.gradeReason: Offer defeat as comfort. The nihilist's gift-wrapped product. Immediately performable and chillingly real.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical illustration. Subject: certain defeat presented in gift box as cozy relief from ambiguity. Mood: nihilistic comfort.

cards.power: Hand the citizen a permission slip to do nothing, signed by themselves.
cards.lore: In learned helplessness, the belief in no-exit outlasts the actual trap.
cards.gradeReason: Permission slip to do nothing, self-signed. The bureaucracy of surrender. Perfect G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: legal satire. Subject: citizen signing their own permission slip for inaction, notarized by despair. Mood: learned helplessness.

cards.power: Supply a face for the formless fear; faces sell better than systems.
cards.lore: Moral panics cast groups as threats, amplified far larger than the actual risk.
cards.gradeReason: Supply the face. You are the fear-retailer. Formless to face is the exact move to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda parody. Subject: amorphous fear given convenient face by authority, sold at retail. Mood: manufactured menace.

cards.power: Sort people into the danger and the decent, and erase the overlap.
cards.lore: Stereotypes are cheap pictures handed to a crowd when checking reality is too slow.
cards.gradeReason: Sort, categorize, erase nuance. Three-step othering procedure. Player becomes the sorter instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: sorting machine dividing crowd into danger/decent bins, overlap shredded. Mood: tribal manufacture.

cards.power: Bind the crowd with a shared enemy; it works faster than a shared plan.
cards.lore: Arbitrary groups turn hostile fast, united by hate until given a shared task.
cards.gradeReason: Bind via enemy. Player is the crowd-welder. Faster than a plan is the operative fact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical illustration. Subject: disparate crowd fused instantly by shared enemy target. Mood: manufactured cohesion.

cards.power: When one enemy stops, issue the next; the slot matters, the face does not.
cards.lore: Propaganda systems maintain a job opening for the enemy that is endlessly refilled.
cards.gradeReason: The slot matters, not the face. Player is the villain-slot manager. Chilling systemic clarity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: WANTED poster parody. Subject: villain slot with question-mark face, endless refill queue behind it. Mood: institutional enemy management.

cards.power: Keep the threat response warm; a scared mind is a steerable mind.
cards.lore: Alarm triggers via a fast subcortical pathway before the thinking brain can assess the threat.
cards.gradeReason: Keep it warm. You are the thermostat of fear. Scared equals steerable. Disturbingly precise.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: fear thermostat kept at warm by unseen operator; toad-brain bypassed. Mood: biological manipulation.

cards.power: Sell the cortisol spike, then sell the relief, to the exact same customer.
cards.lore: Chronic activation of the stress response degrades health and judgment over time.
cards.gradeReason: Sell spike, sell relief, same customer. The darkest business model in the deck. Immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark economics. Subject: cortisol spike and relief both sold to same exhausted customer at vending machine. Mood: biological arbitrage.

cards.power: Use fear to shrink attention to the next ten seconds; long plans die there.
cards.lore: Under high arousal, attention narrows to the threat, losing peripheral info and long horizons.
cards.gradeReason: Shrink to ten seconds. Long plans die. You are the attention-narrower. Strategic precision.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink satirical. Subject: fear tunnel shrinking vision to ten-second keyhole, horizon gone. Mood: cognitive capture.

cards.power: Frighten people, then offer whoever promises to make it stop.
cards.lore: When mortality is salient, people lean harder toward strong authority and in-group certainty.
cards.gradeReason: Frighten, then offer the savior. The full political loop in nine words. Flawless.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda parody. Subject: frightened crowd reaching toward figure who promises to stop the alarm. Mood: fear-compliance loop.

cards.power: Promote the vivid single case to the status of a pattern.
cards.lore: A memorable, frightening story outweighs boring statistics even when the stat is the truth.
cards.gradeReason: Promote the vivid case. You are the pattern-inflater. Immediate editorial operator role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: single vivid case promoted to full-pattern billboard, base rate invisible. Mood: statistical sleight of hand.

cards.power: Show the scary number; hide what it is out of.
cards.lore: People ignore base rates and react to raw counts, making rare events feel common.
cards.gradeReason: Show number, hide denominator. One of the cleanest dark moves in the deck. Instantly enacted.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical infographic. Subject: giant numerator displayed, denominator hidden behind curtain. Mood: manufactured alarm.

cards.power: Keep the frames that confirm the dread; quietly drop the rest.
cards.lore: Selective reporting builds a false overall picture where every individual fact checks out.
cards.gradeReason: Keep confirming frames, drop the rest quietly. Player is the silent curator of dread.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial illustration. Subject: cherry-picker selecting red cherries, disconfirming evidence falling silently below. Mood: selective reality.

cards.power: Repeat a story until it feels true, so nobody asks for the actual rate.
cards.lore: Leading with what bleeds trains an audience to drastically overestimate danger.
cards.gradeReason: Repeat until felt. Nobody asks for the rate. Repetition as statistical replacement. Sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: media parody. Subject: repeated story calcifying into felt fact, actual rate invisible below. Mood: narrative calcification.

cards.power: Hold the body at low-grade threat for months; never let it stand down.
cards.lore: Allostatic load is the cumulative physical wear from chronic stress systems left running.
cards.gradeReason: Hold body at low-grade threat, months on end, no stand-down. Player is the body-alarm keeper.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medical-editorial. Subject: body held in permanent low-level threat posture, never standing down. Mood: chronic alert exhaustion.

cards.power: Keep the breathing high and tight; calm thinking requires the lower lungs.
cards.lore: Threat shifts breathing to rapid/shallow, blocking the calm parasympathetic state.
cards.gradeReason: Physiological mechanism described well, but player role (who keeps whose breathing high?) needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anatomical satire. Subject: tight high breathing blocking lower-lung calm state, parasympathetic pathway severed. Mood: physiological capture.

cards.power: Run the engine without a cooldown until it loses the ability to idle.
cards.lore: Sustained stress without recovery is the core physiological driver of burnout.
cards.gradeReason: Metaphorical engine instruction needs slight unpacking — player as mechanic-of-burnout is implied, not named.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mechanical editorial. Subject: engine running on fumes without cooldown, idle function gone. Mood: systemic burnout.

cards.power: Let exhaustion read as apathy; blame the victim for the depletion you farmed.
cards.lore: Withdrawal is the predictable symptom of a nervous system held in alarm too long.
cards.gradeReason: Farm depletion, then blame victim for it. The most devastating card in the chapter. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical portrait. Subject: farmed-exhausted citizen labelled LAZY, depletion farmer standing behind. Mood: manufactured apathy.

cards.power: Present the system as total, with absolutely no outside to step into.
cards.lore: Hypernormalisation is treating fakeness as normal because alternatives seem unimaginable.
cards.gradeReason: Present the system as absolute. Player knows exactly what to do: seal the room, call it the world.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surrealist editorial. Subject: total system with all exits bricked over, fakeness labeled as reality. Mood: hypernormalized enclosure.

cards.power: Repeat that no alternative exists until imagining one feels inherently naive.
cards.lore: TINA converts a political choice into a fake law of nature (capitalist realism).
cards.gradeReason: Repeat until imagining becomes naive. TINA as performance script. One of the deck's best.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda parody. Subject: TINA sign installed as law of nature, political choice buried beneath. Mood: choice disguised as physics.

cards.power: Run enough failed attempts that the animal stops trying long before the door opens.
cards.lore: Expectation, not the cage, holds subjects long after escape becomes possible.
cards.gradeReason: Run enough failure to kill trying. Door stays open; habit has closed. Crisp behavioral move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: behavioral satire. Subject: cage door open, animal inside having long stopped trying to leave. Mood: learned helplessness.

cards.power: Make every exit look childish, so nobody is caught wanting one.
cards.lore: Ridicule polices the boundary of the thinkable without requiring actual counterarguments.
cards.gradeReason: Make exits childish. Nobody caught wanting one. Ridicule as boundary police. Immediate and sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: raven mocking every exit door with childish label, alternatives shamed away. Mood: ridicule as governance.

cards.power: Trade the burden of choosing for the comfort of being driven.
cards.lore: An external locus of control predicts a total failure to attempt influencing one's life.
cards.gradeReason: Trade burden for comfort of being driven. Player performs the handover. Precise and embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial illustration. Subject: driver sliding from wheel to passenger seat, comfort replacing agency. Mood: chosen captivity.

cards.power: Let the feed decide what is true so you never carry the doubt yourself.
cards.lore: When judgment is fully outsourced, the capacity to weigh evidence atrophies.
cards.gradeReason: Let feed carry the doubt. Player performs the outsourcing. The doubt-delegation card. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical portrait. Subject: feed deciding truth while owner sits empty-handed, doubt outsourced. Mood: delegated judgment.

cards.power: A faculty that never decides forgets how to decide.
cards.lore: Decision follows a use-it-or-lose-it principle; switched off, the habit weakens.
cards.gradeReason: States what happens to the will — diagnostic description rather than direct performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anatomical satire. Subject: will-muscle shrunken from disuse, decision-pathway overgrown with weeds. Mood: voluntary atrophy.

cards.power: Present the total gently, years after the choice was quietly made for you.
cards.lore: The cost of surrendered agency is billed in years spent watching instead of acting.
cards.gradeReason: Present the total gently, years later. Temporal precision and the gentleness make this devastating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: accounting satire. Subject: decade-delayed invoice for surrendered agency, gently slipped under door. Mood: deferred reckoning.

cards.power: Mark everything as breaking; let absolutely nothing be allowed to finish.
cards.lore: The continuous news cycle creates a permanent present where resolution kills engagement.
cards.gradeReason: Mark everything BREAKING; nothing finishes. Player is the resolution-killer. Instantly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: news parody. Subject: BREAKING banner hung permanently over everything, resolution banned. Mood: perpetual present.

cards.power: Never ask anything of the reader; an absence of an off-ramp is the tell.
cards.lore: Genuine information equips action; retention-feeds offer no point to act and leave.
cards.gradeReason: Never give the reader an exit. Absence of off-ramp is the signature. Diagnostic-as-action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: road sign satire. Subject: all media exits replaced with NO EXIT signs, antelope kept circling. Mood: designed captivity.

cards.power: Build a fear that no amount of evidence can ever resolve.
cards.lore: A dread that survives reassuring fact was never actually about the facts.
cards.gradeReason: Build evidence-proof fear. Player is the unfalsifiable-dread architect. Cold precision.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic editorial. Subject: dread surviving armored against all reassuring facts, vault of the unfalsifiable. Mood: evidence-proof anxiety.

cards.power: Watch whether the story ever resolves; if it only renews, you found the mechanism.
cards.lore: Tracking if narrative closes is a reliable way to tell reporting from retention.
cards.gradeReason: Watch for resolution vs. renewal. Player becomes the loop-tester. Counter-intelligence role built in.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: analytical illustration. Subject: ouroboros story renewing without resolving, mechanism labeled for inspection. Mood: diagnostic clarity.

cards.power: Trace who gets paid while you stay still—in attention, power, or deferred reform.
cards.lore: Following the payout explains structural patterns that individual intentions cannot.
cards.gradeReason: Trace the payout while you're still. Analyst role activated. Cui bono as a move, not a question.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: investigative editorial. Subject: payout trail mapped from citizen stillness to beneficiary wallets. Mood: structural revelation.

cards.power: Name the parties for whom your inaction is the desired outcome, not a side effect.
cards.lore: Diffuse incentives can farm mass paralysis without anyone conspiring to do so.
cards.gradeReason: Name who profits from your inaction. One of the sharpest analytical moves in the whole corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: economic satire. Subject: invisible beneficiaries harvesting mass inaction dividend, no conspiracy required. Mood: diffuse exploitation.

cards.power: Notice that the smallest real action breaks the spell faster than the largest when informed.
cards.lore: Agency is recovered through physical doing, not through being better informed.
cards.gradeReason: 'Notice' is an observational verb — invites reflection more than immediate embodied performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial illustration. Subject: tiny real action cracking vast spell, largest informed idea doing nothing. Mood: unexpected agency.

cards.power: Ask this of every alarm before you forward it: who benefits when you stop acting?
cards.lore: The collapse may be real, but separating genuine danger from manufactured stillness is the cure.
cards.gradeReason: Ask before forwarding: who benefits from your stillness? The deck's master key. Flawless closer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: investigative editorial. Subject: magnifying glass held to every alarm asking 'who profits from your stillness?' Mood: clarifying confrontation.

verdict: Anatomy of a Trap is the sharpest deck FrizzleBob has fielded — a forensic dissection of how manufactured fear, weaponized attention, and structured hopelessness actually work, card by card. Fourteen chapters cover every mechanism from the Cortisol Economy to the Quiet Invoice with clinical precision and immediate performability: 86% G1, zero G3. The one structural gap is The Firehose (card 9), which carries no POWER/LORE text — a daring design choice that performs its own concept but leaves the table without an instruction set. Table-ready: YES — this is the flagship exhibition anchor.
blurb: The full operating manual for manufacturing hopelessness — 56 cards naming every mechanism that keeps you scared, sorted, and still. For anyone who suspects the apocalypse is being sold to them.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob with scissors amid panic-media TVs is immediately arresting and on-brand
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — IGNORE DYSTOPIA is paradoxical, memorable, and perfectly sets the ironic register
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Cover chaos matches the deck's forensic-satirical tone exactly
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Strong FrizzleBob visual language; format is recognizable but content is fresh
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Exhibition visitors will photograph this; tagline is shareable
coverQA.coverNote: The cover lands the paradox of the deck's title immediately — you're being invited to ignore something that's already screaming at you. 'Cut the doomscroll and play some comics, fluffhead!' as bottom-of-cover CTA is gold. The scissors are the right visual metaphor for what this deck does to media fear.

notes: Exhibition deck for Hannover 5 Jul 2026, Deck B / DYSTOPIA slot. 14-chapter structure, each spread naming a manipulation mechanism. Chapter titles function as mini-essays in themselves. Card 9 (The Firehose) intentionally carries no POWER/LORE text — the visual IS the content. Grade distribution is heavily G1-skewed (86%) reflecting exceptional writing quality rather than calibration error. Companion old JSON: ANATOMY_OF_A_TRAP_web_H.pdf.json. Cover tagline: 'The apocalypse will be televised. Repeatedly. On a loop. With ads.'

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: IGNORE DYSTOPIA – Fifty-Six Cards That Name Every Trick Selling You the Apocalypse (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

The end of the world is a product. Somebody has a quota, and your attention is the currency they bill.

Fear is not weather that rolls in on its own. It is manufactured, metered, and invoiced. The Cortisol Economy runs on your nervous system the way an engine runs on fuel: keep the dread topped up and you stay scared, sorted, and still, which is exactly where a frightened person is most profitable and least trouble. The Quiet Invoice is the line you never see itemized, the toll the panic charges you in sleep, nerve, and the years you spend bracing for a collapse that is mostly someone's content calendar. This is the IGNORE wing of the Hannover triptych, the panel in the middle that refuses to feed the machine. Ignore here does not mean look away from what is real. It means stop paying the fear its rent.

This is Social Story Wrestling run as a counter-interrogation. You read a card aloud, the table performs the mechanism it names instead of arguing about it, and the doom that was working you so smoothly has to stand in the light and show how the trick is done.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Ignore Dystopia Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Cortisol Economy (the business model that runs on your dread and needs you anxious to stay solvent), The Quiet Invoice (the bill the panic charges you in sleep and nerve, never itemized, always paid), and The Core Question you carry off the table, the one that asks what the fear is actually for and who collects on it.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the part where every card can claim anything until the room calls the bluff. Cut on the dotted lines, shuffle, and start the match.
- The Trap Anatomy: fourteen chapters, four cards each, every spread dissecting one mechanism of manufactured hopelessness, from the first staged alarm to The Firehose, the card that floods you with so much at once that the picture is the only thing left standing.

This wing hangs in the middle of the triptych. Forget clears the rescue fantasy off the wall on the left, Embrace picks up the pencil on the right, and Ignore stands between them and cuts the dread that keeps you from doing either. Read a column straight down and one question gets three answers. The whole triptych lives at protopians.substack.com. Stop paying the panic, bring the cards, and make the apocalypse show you its invoice.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"An apocalypse with a release schedule is not a forecast. It is a subscription, and you are allowed to cancel."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
